---
applyTo: "db/migrate/**/*.rb"
---

# Database Migration Code Review Rules

Reference: `db/migrate/`, `db/structure.sql`, `db/enterprise_structure.sql`.

## Conventions

Migrations should be generated with `script/generate-migration <Name>` (a thin wrapper around `bundle exec rails g migration`). Verify the migration matches the generated template:

- File header is `# frozen_string_literal: true`.
- Class name matches the generated PascalCase name and is `<Name> < ActiveRecord::Migration[<version>]`. Use the latest `[version]` available in the codebase (currently `7.2`); don't downgrade.
- Body is a `change` method (or explicit `up`/`down` when reversibility requires it).
- Don't hand-write a migration file from scratch — use the generator so the timestamp, class name, and base class version stay consistent.

Other conventions:

- One logical change per migration. Don't combine an `add_column` with a backfill loop.
- For multiple alterations to a single table, issue separate statements (e.g., several `add_column` calls in one `change` method). The `Rails/NoBulkChangeTable` cop (`lib/rubocop/cop/rails/no_bulk_change_table.rb`) bans `change_table ..., bulk: true` because of a Rails bug with `table_name_prefix` in enterprise mode (see [rails/rails#56573](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/56573)). Don't suggest `bulk: true`.
- **No application logic in migrations.** A migration body should be database schema changes only. Anything that reads or mutates app data — backfills, repairs, computed columns — belongs in a transition under `lib/dependabot/transitions/` (see `transitions.instructions.md`). The only exception is invoking a transition from the migration to run it on GHES (see "Data migrations" below).

## Safety

- **Reversibility**: prefer `change` for simple operations. For data-loss operations or anything Rails can't auto-reverse, define explicit `up`/`down`.
- **Indexes**: any new foreign key column, lookup column, or column used in `WHERE`/`ORDER BY` should get an index. Flag missing indexes in review.
- **Charset/collation**: when creating a new table, follow the existing `utf8mb4` / collation conventions seen in nearby migrations.
- **Locking**: large tables should not get `add_column ..., default: ...` without `null: true` first — defaults can rewrite the whole table on MySQL.
- **Renames** (`rename_column`, `rename_table`) are dangerous on hot tables. Prefer add-new + dual-write + backfill + drop-old across multiple PRs.
- **Large text/JSON/blob columns**: think twice before adding a `text`, `json`, `mediumtext`, or `blob` column to an existing model. Large columns slow down full-model fetches and bloat replica replication. Ask what the data is used for and whether it should live in blob storage (S3, Azure Blob) with a small reference column instead.

## Data migrations

- **Backfills, repairs, and any data mutation belong in a transition**, not in the migration body and not in a background job. See `transitions.instructions.md`.
- **Why transitions and not background jobs**: transitions are self-contained scripts checked in alongside the migration. They include a point-in-time snapshot of the model classes they need, so they keep working even after app code drifts. A background job runs against whatever is on `main` at the time it runs — fine for cloud, but on GHES the gap between the migration and the next deploy can be months, and the model the job expects may no longer exist or may have changed shape.
- **The migration body is allowed to invoke the transition** when GHES needs the backfill at upgrade time (cloud usually runs the transition out-of-band via chatops). Pattern: `Dependabot::Transitions::SomeBackfill.new(dry_run: false).perform if Dependabot.enterprise?`. Reference: `db/migrate/20260118191643_run_current_state_backfill_on_ghes.rb`.
- **Truly small** one-off data fixes (< ~100 rows, fixed bound) are OK inline if they don't reference application code beyond the model itself.

## Schema sync

- Both `db/structure.sql` and `db/enterprise_structure.sql` should be regenerated when migrations land. If a migration PR touches one but not the other, ask why.

## Reviewer checklist

- Migration file is generated by `script/generate-migration` (matches the Rails generator template — frozen-string-literal header, PascalCase class name matching the filename, latest `ActiveRecord::Migration[version]`).
- Migration is single-purpose and has a clear `change` or `up`/`down`.
- New columns intended for lookup/sorting have indexes.
- Charset/collation matches existing conventions.
- Migration body contains schema changes only — no application logic. Backfills are invoked via a transition, not inline and not via a background job.
- New large text/JSON/blob columns are justified — would blob storage be a better fit?
- Only database schema changes and performing transitions are allowed in the migration body. A single migration may do one or the other but not both.
- `db/structure.sql` (and enterprise variant) updated.
